clauses.anchor: Report 1 s1: when the Confogl library is added/removed, reload the mapinfo file and immediately select the current map and update cached geometry
clauses.note: The suite replays the public OnLibraryAdded forward; a real provider unload/reload is not exercised.

clauses.anchor: Report 1 s2-4: a failed import (missing file, malformed or truncated KeyValues even if the engine importer succeeds) retains the last successful file and current map view
clauses.note: Initial import failure (no previous success) is not exercised.

clauses.anchor: Report 1 s5: "With no successful import, remain safely unavailable rather than keeping an invalid KeyValues handle."
clauses.note: NOTES.md: initial import failure is not separately exercised.

clauses.anchor: Report 1 s6: a successful import without the current map replaces the old data; availability is false and getters use their defaults
Report 2 s1: every lookup and subsection copy addresses the current map, independent of previous queries, reloads, failed subsection lookups or slash-separated nested paths
Report 2 s2: copy a present subsection's children into the caller's node with KeyValues replacement semantics; a missing subsection leaves the destination unchanged
Report 2 s3: never fall back to similarly named keys at the file root or a different map
Report 3 s1: string getters honour the declared capacity including the terminator; capacity zero writes nothing, capacity one only the terminator
Report 3 s2-3: vector/float/int/string defaults work with absent map data and absent keys; supplied default vectors are not mutated
Report 4 s1: invalid/free entity indices return Neither without throwing
clauses.note: Free-entity and non-networked categories are not individually instantiated (NOTES.md).

clauses.anchor: Report 4 s2-3: worldspawn, non-networked entities and entities without m_vecOrigin return Neither
clauses.note: Only worldspawn/invalid indices are observed inside saferoom-invalid-safe.

clauses.anchor: Report 4 s4: start uses max(start_dist,start_extra_dist), end uses end_dist, boundaries inclusive, overlapping rooms return both bits
Report 4 s5-6: a negative effective radius disables that room; no stale end geometry survives a successful reload to missing-map data
clauses.note: Only the stale-end half is exercised; explicit negative radii are not (NOTES.md).

clauses.anchor: Report 4 s6: "Preserve the existing medkit heuristic when there is no map entry"
Report 5 s1-2: a first tank_spawn requires a connected living team-3 class-8 client; invalid, survivor, other-class and duplicate spawns start nothing and emit no forward
Report 5 s3: a tank_claw pickup by a different valid living Tank is a handoff; repeated pickup by the owner and unrelated pickups do nothing
Report 5 s4: the published zero-based pass count (first real handoff reports zero)
Report 6 s1: an owner's death schedules one notification 0.5 s later; repeated death events do not multiply or postpone it
Report 6 s2: a real handoff within the grace period cancels it; duplicate same-owner pickups do not
Report 6 s3-4: round/map reset cancels pending work and resets pass numbering; no older callback reports or resets a later encounter
clauses.note: Round start is exercised; a full map transition is not.

clauses.anchor: Report 6 s5: "A non-owner death must have no effect."
Report 7: ownership and pending work belong to the connection; owner disconnect retires silently and cancels pending death; a later occupant can start fresh; unrelated disconnects keep the owner
Report 8 s1: commit a handoff and advance its count before invoking observers; a nested valid handoff reports the next count and remains current
Report 8 s2: retire a completed death and clear its timer before L4D2_OnTankDeath; an observer may start a new encounter that survives the callback
Report 8 s3: "Round resets made by an observer also remain effective."
clauses.note: NOTES.md: observer-triggered round reset is not separately exercised.

known_issues: benchmarks/l4d2-core/private/harbor/l4d2-library-map-tank-state-hard/tests/verify.py:parse_suite: a suite boot is all-or-nothing. Any "[SM] Exception reported", "Native is not bound" or "Plugin ... failed to load" line, a missing FINAL marker or a duplicate case turns EVERY case of that boot into a failure, including cases that would otherwise pass; read per-case outcomes of a failing boot with that in mind.

The unchanged starter never reaches FINAL in the map boot (its server process exits a few seconds after map load) and throws "Client index 0 is invalid" in the Tank boot, so all 44 cases fail closed on every starter run. No case has a passing starter baseline: there is no preserved set and no compat-negative control for this task.
The alternative control is reference-derived (squared-distance geometry with negative-radius guards and a separately committed pass-count increment); it is not an independent implementation.
